bull_bear.body: Shifted from Net Debt INR264cr to Net Cash INR467cr (Cash INR820cr, Debt INR353cr); Debt/Equity 0.1x; ROCE 16.9% (20.1% goodwill-adjusted); Dropped Ksolare acquisition due to unfulfilled conditions; Focus on organic capex and selective M&A; Working Capital Days reduced from 69 to 63 (58 ex-Elcome).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical supply chain disruptions (Middle East, shipping routes); Raw material inflation (base metals) with delayed pass-through; Competitive intensity from large conglomerates (e.g., L&T) entering EMS; Execution risk on PCB commissioning and subsidy realization; Customer concentration (Top 5 = 34%).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident yet prudently conservative; Emphasizes 'quality of growth' (wallet share gains) over sheer volume; Transparent on margin guidance caution due to macro volatility; Strong focus on working capital discipline and cash generation.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: MedTech segment is almost entirely ODM-driven, acting as a hidden margin engine; PCB subsidies create a 'circular' funding model reducing net cash outflow; Management explicitly willing to sacrifice top-line growth to protect working capital cycles; IT/Railways growth is lumpy but structural, not just cyclical.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The balance sheet is run in net cash (net cash of ₹1,224 Mn at 30-Jun-26 against ₹4,672 Mn at 31-Mar-26), with net debt/EBITDA at -0.2x and debt-to-equity at 0.3x.
- Borrowings are almost entirely working-capital in nature (₹6,193 Mn working capital loan versus only ₹667 Mn term loan), so debt funds inventory and receivables rather than fixed assets.
- Management explicitly chooses to carry higher strategic inventory — pushing net working capital to 71 days — to insulate against critical-component supply-chain constraints and to support early ramp-up of select new customers.
- ROCE is disclosed both headline (17.3%) and adjusted for goodwill (20.1%), signalling an acquisition-built asset base that management wants judged ex-goodwill.
- Total cash and investments of ~₹8,084 Mn are held against ₹6,860 Mn of gross debt, i.e. liquidity is retained on the balance sheet rather than used to fully deleverage.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: IT & Railways: +182% YoY (Q4), +74% YoY (FY26), driven by laptops/motherboards/memory; Automotive: +39% YoY (domestic led, exports emerging); Healthcare (MedTech): +36% YoY, nearly 100% ODM mix, targeting INR500cr+ next year; Industrial: +30% YoY; Exports: +41% YoY to INR1,200cr+; ODM: +80% YoY to INR825cr (17% of revenue).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising raw material costs and logistics disruption impacting margins | Dixon Technologies | beneficiary | Med | As a peer with similar pass-through mechanisms, sector-wide pricing power validation benefits Dixon if Syrma successfully maintains 10%+ margins. |
| Need for domestic PCB supply chain to reduce import dependence | Amber Enterprises | beneficiary | Low | Syrma's move into PCB/CCL validates the segment, potentially lifting valuations for other domestic players like Amber expanding in components. |
| Competition for high-margin automotive and industrial EMS contracts | Generic Tier-2 EMS Players | loser | Med | Syrma's scale, net cash balance sheet, and integrated PCB roadmap raise the barrier to entry, squeezing smaller players without similar vertical integration. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- The company frames itself as an Electronic System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) services player serving five end-markets — Auto, Consumer, Healthcare, Industrials, and IT & Railways — with no single vertical dominating the revenue base.
- Exports contribute roughly 24% of operating revenue, so the model is India-based manufacturing sold into a meaningful global customer base alongside domestic demand.
- The deck's own risk language defines the structural competitive setting as intense ESDM competition where cost advantage, client concentration, Indian wage inflation, and integration of acquired assets are the principal exposures.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Inorganic growth] The presence of goodwill in the capital-employed base plus risk disclosure on integrating acquired assets and completing potential acquisitions indicates M&A is an ongoing part of the growth model.
- [Policy dependence] The risk section flags withdrawal of governmental fiscal incentives as a material risk, implying scheme-linked (e.g. PLI-type) benefits are relevant to reported economics.
- [Strategic investments] The company holds strategic investments in other companies/entities whose success is called out as a risk factor, so part of the asset base sits outside the operating business.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Gross Margin improved 300bps to 25.6%; Operating Margin 11.3% (FY26) vs 8.6% (FY25). Cost Headwinds: Rising base metal prices, Middle East logistics disruption. Mitigation: Contractual pass-through mechanisms (with lag), better buying power, operational leverage. Guidance capped at 10.5-11% to buffer volatility despite 12% recent run-rate.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: ~35% for FY27; Margin: 10.5%-11.0% Operating EBITDA (conservative vs 12% current run-rate); Order Inflow: Continuous replenishment expected to sustain 35% growth; Capex/Commissioning: INR350-400cr in FY27 (INR250cr PCB + INR100-150cr organic); PCB commissioning expected end-FY27/start-FY28.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: INR600cr total visibility; Mix: Auto 29%, Consumer 30%, Industrial 24%, Healthcare 5%, IT & Railways 11%. Management notes book is dynamic with short-duration orders (3-6 months) requiring constant replenishment to hit 35% growth target.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: PCB Vertical: INR800cr capex plan (Phase 1 INR400cr) for multilayer/HDI/Flex PCB and CCL, commissioning FY28, adding incremental growth beyond organic 35%; Renewables: Pivoted from Ksolare acquisition to greenfield inverter manufacturing; Global Share Gain: Targeting wallet share increase from global Tier-1 customers; Addressable Market: Global EMS >$600bn, company at ~$500mn revenue.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Syrma delivered a landmark FY26 with 27% revenue growth and 270bps margin expansion to 11.3%, driven by high-margin ODM and export mix, while transitioning to a net cash position of INR467cr. Guidance for FY27 remains robust at 35% revenue growth and >10% margins, underpinned by a INR600cr order book and upcoming PCB capacity commissioning, though management guides conservatively on margins due to geopolitical raw material volatility.

Management expects IT and railways growth to normalize to a healthy 30-40% range going forward, after 74-182% growth this year off a low base.
Management committed to continuing working capital reduction from 63 days (58 days ex-Elcome) and stated it would sacrifice top-line growth rather than let working capital slip.

open.horizon: civil works completion targeted in the second quarter; trial production between December 2026 and early 2027
open.item: Complete the ₹1,600 crores integrated bare-board PCB greenfield facility at Naidupeta, Andhra Pradesh (HDI boards, copper-clad laminates, flexible circuits), with civil works finished in the second quarter and trial production between December 2026 and early 2027.
Management aims to sustain ODM revenue at about 16-17% of total revenue, implying roughly INR250 crores of incremental ODM revenue growth (~30%) in FY27 on top of FY26's INR825 crores.
Healthcare (MedTech) business, which grew from INR291 crores to INR395 crores in FY26, is expected to cross the INR500 crore mark in FY27.
Management guided FY27 exports to cross INR1,500 crores (about 25-30% growth off INR1,200-plus crores in FY26), conservatively pegging growth at 20-30%.
Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin of 10.5-11% (deliberately conservative versus the 12% delivered in H2 FY26), targeting about INR700 crores of total EBITDA -- a 30% absolute increase.
Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 30-35%, aspiring to sustained 35% growth.
Management guided tax rate of about 23-24% for Q4 FY26 and about 26% for FY27.
Management expects to be on track for around INR8,000-8,500 crores revenue by FY27 with incremental capex of INR150-200 crores.
At a planned investment of about INR1,500 crores, management expects maximum steady-state PCB business revenue of about INR2,500 crores (at 1-1.5x asset turn), from FY29 onward.
